notes: Under A131 (CTO Ruling 11) a crime victim decides whether to report from their own side: the offense, against the trouble of reporting; whether an offense has been recorded against them before (repeat victimization, sliding with the count); their own past reports and past charges; their temperament (reliability plus conflict) and their age. Knowing the offender is no longer a weight. The weights are placeholders in UNRESEARCHED_REPORTING (src/simulation/crime/reporting.ts), set so a drawn town's totals sit near the 2022 and 2023 NCVS shares reported: robbery 64.0 and 42.4 percent, assault 40.6 and 44.9 percent, burglary 44.9 and 42.2 percent.

The national survey does not show that a close tie lowers reporting. Nonfatal Domestic Violence, 2003-2012 (NCJ 244697, table 8): intimate partner 56 percent, immediate family 56, other relatives 49, acquaintances 39, strangers 49. Criminal Victimization, 2023 (NCJ 309335, table 4): domestic violence 53.8 percent in 2022 and 47.7 in 2023, against stranger violence 36.0 and 44.9. Those shares check the town's totals by relationship; they never decide one victim.

Still open: the acquaintance group reports less than strangers or family in the survey, and nothing in the weighing yet produces that; the survey's mix of simple assaults among acquaintances is the likely reason, and the world records no injury or loss for an offense, so harm is read from the offense alone.
Vandalism has no share reported in the NCVS reports checked; its harm weight sits with other theft (26.4 and 24.8 percent) and is not checked against a total.
question: With the offense's seriousness held equal, how much do injury, loss, repeat victimization, the victim's earlier contact with police (as a reporter and as someone charged), their age and their temperament change the odds that they report a crime to police, and why do victims of acquaintances report less?

title: Why crime victims report to police, or keep quiet
usableAnswer: Adjusted odds ratios (or shares with seriousness held equal) for reporting by victim-offender relationship, the victim's age, and the victim's earlier police contact, from a named NCVS analysis or comparable survey, so each placeholder weight can be read as data.
whyItMatters: Whether a crime reaches the police log decides what the local paper, the police and the prosecutor ever see, and a player who changes a town's ties or its police changes who reports.
